records.quote: this coming morning at ten to seven, I took--and will take--the machine and I traveled back to ten to five yesterday afternoon
records.paraphrase: Benji describes traveling backward in time from the coming morning to the previous afternoon.

records.quote: With this added power, the machine can travel five years. Five years at a jump
records.paraphrase: A new special power line lets the machine jump five years at a time.

records.quote: there I was resting comfortably on a small cloud in far outer space, watching a great spiral nebula whirling in infinite majesty through the vast, empty blackness
records.paraphrase: After touching the machine, the narrator experiences a vision of outer space and a spiral nebula.

records.quote: But just now the machine is there twice. That creates further static force fields.
records.paraphrase: Benji explains the machine appears doubled because it exists twice, creating extra force fields.

records.quote: it is a fact that I am in two places at the same time--only on different circuits
records.paraphrase: Benji claims to exist simultaneously in two places due to time travel.

records.quote: So I couldn't possibly have driven your car up the steps and through the glass doors into the ancient history section of the museum.
records.paraphrase: Benji plans to use his simultaneous presence as an alibi for crimes committed by his time-traveling double.

records.quote: It should be obvious. I have built a time machine.
records.paraphrase: Benji declares he has constructed a time machine.

records.quote: I have had all electric power lines removed from that entire section of the house. There is no power. None.
records.paraphrase: The narrator removes all electric power so Benji's machine cannot escape when it reappears.

records.quote: More or less, it is a matter of setting up the proper number of counteracting magnetic force fields, properly focused, in a proper relationship each with the other to bend the normal space factors in such a way as to circumvent time.
records.paraphrase: Benji explains the machine works by arranging counteracting magnetic force fields to bend space and circumvent time.

records.quote: He fiddled with a dial or knob--and vanished. The double exposure look of the machine disappeared too.
records.paraphrase: One version of Benji operates the machine and vanishes, along with its doubled appearance.

records.quote: No, Bull. Not a machine for telling time; a machine for traveling through time or, actually, more or less around it.
records.paraphrase: Benji clarifies the device is for traveling through time rather than measuring it.

records.quote: The amount or period of time is a question of power. With only the regular house current I have connected now, about a day at a step is the limit.
records.paraphrase: The distance of a time jump depends on available power; house current allows about a day per jump.

records.quote: "Benji, it was _true_ then! All that you were telling me about going through time was true!
records.paraphrase: Daisy realizes with astonishment that the time travel was real.

records.quote: Benji twisted a knob and grinned. "Good-by now," he said. And they were gone.
records.paraphrase: Benji and Daisy disappear in the machine after twisting a knob.

records.quote: I am figuring on a little party; a little reception in honor of our first intrepid time traveler. A surprise party.
records.paraphrase: The narrator plans a trap timed to Benji's predicted reappearance from time travel.

records.quote: Benji will work his dials and controls, frantically. Nothing will happen. No power.
records.paraphrase: The narrator predicts Benji will be trapped because his machine will have no power to leave.

records.quote: His story was unbelievable. But I was beginning to believe it--partly because of the machine there and the fact that I had seen two of him practically at once the evening before
records.paraphrase: The narrator gradually accepts Benji's claim after seeing evidence of the doubled Benji.

records.quote: He plodded ahead in the University Physics Department and fiddled around his lab whenever he could escape into it.
records.paraphrase: Benji works as a physicist experimenting in his laboratory.

criteria.rationale: Benji, a university physicist, offers pseudo-scientific explanation of bending space via counteracting magnetic force fields to circumvent time. The science is decorative jargon rather than materially represented natural process, but the invocation of physics/magnetic fields and a physicist's lab supports a plausible speculative-science reading.
The time machine is an engineered invention that drives the entire plot, action, and outcome, including the power-dependent jump distance that becomes the narrator's trap. Central to the story.
Temporal displacement is the core novum: Benji travels back one day and later jumps five years forward, appearing in two places at once. Time travel is causally central throughout.

The story develops consequences from the machine's premise: the five-year power-jump limit and power dependence lead the narrator to strip all electric power so that Benji reappears powerless and trapped exactly five years later. This extrapolation from the established technological rules is central to the resolution.

Although Benji is a physicist and the narrator gradually accepts the machine after seeing evidence, there is no material demonstration of observation, hypothesis, testing, measurement, or evidential revision driving understanding. The machine simply exists and works; the narrator's belief and revenge scheme are not scientific method.

Touching the machine produces a vision of outer space and a spiral nebula, a nonordinary cosmic environment. However, this is a transient hallucination rather than an actual other place or visitors, so materiality is incidental and interpretation uncertain.

The story's harms are personal and comic (a wrecked museum, stolen police car, an unhappy marriage). There is no natural, technological, cosmic, biological, or human-caused large-scale disaster that is actual, impending, remembered, or causally central.

candidates.description: Benji's time machine, a jungle-gym-like apparatus powered by electric current that bends space via counteracting magnetic force fields to travel through (or 'around') time. Jump distance scales with available power: house current yields about a day per jump, a special power line yields five years per jump. It produces observable side effects such as the operator existing in two places at once, doubled 'double-exposure' appearances, and force fields near the rig.

novelty.rationale: The machine introduces a totalizing difference from the empirical norm: genuine travel through time, with an operator existing simultaneously in two places. This is confirmed as real within the storyworld (Daisy's recognition) and alters the fundamental causal structure of the narrated events.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The machine is presented with a coherent, immanent, nonsupernatural logic: built by a working physicist, explained through magnetic force fields bending space to circumvent time, with a systematic power-to-distance rule (house current = one day; special line = five years) that the plot obeys consistently. The account is deliberately technobabble-light, but Suvinian cognitive validation requires coherent immanent logic rather than engineering accuracy, and the rules are applied consistently and drive events.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The machine governs the entire narrative logic: it enables the doubled-Benji alibi scheme, drives the escape of Benji and Daisy, causes the narrator to be trapped into marrying Vera, and sets up the five-year-delayed revenge trap predicated on the machine's predictable reappearance and its dependence on electric power. The whole plot and its resolution depend on the machine's rules.

estrangement.rationale: Reader-facing contrast: the mundane domestic-comedy setting is estranged by a working time machine whose operator appears doubled and exists on 'different circuits.' Storyworld consequences are decisive: theft of a car and police car, the marriage entrapment, and the power-deprivation trap. Character reactions (the narrator's gradual belief, Daisy's dawning realization) register the estrangement without being required for the adjudication.
